question: How much insurgent reproductive/organizational activity is suppressed per unit of incremental public-development spending, how does that return vary by allocation rule and dose, and how much suppression persists after the spending intervention ends?

cost_accounting.primary_denominator: incremental nominal public-development outflow versus the 1x dose under the same allocation mode
cost_accounting.normalized_reporting_unit: 1,200 Pineland capital units = 1% of the default one-month 120,000 federal policy-budget ceiling
cost_accounting.real_dollar_conversion: If the real-dollar monthly budget anchor is B dollars, then one Pineland capital unit corresponds to B/120000 dollars. No B is assumed in this assay.

analysis_rules: Use within-seed 1x same-mode baselines for dose ROI so allocation-rule differences are not mixed into the spending denominator.
At each fixed budget multiplier, compare allocation modes against equal-locality using paired seeds; this is a budget-neutral allocation-efficiency comparison.
Report suppression per 1,200 incremental public capital separately for each insurgent outcome; do not collapse outcomes into one utility score.
Report intervention-end effect and final-day retained effect separately. A transient improvement that reverses after spending ends is not durable suppression.
Fail closed for an outcome when the denominator is nonpositive or the 1x baseline has already lost the relevant insurgent state in most seeds.
No real-world dollar or operational COIN effect size may be claimed from internal capital units without an external calibration contract.
interpretation_guard: Synthetic mechanism experiment on persistent low-tempo live-insurgency support. It tests model economics and causal pathways, not real-world aid effectiveness or operational targeting.
